title: Best Time to Paint a House Exterior in Houston, TX (2026)
description: The best time to paint a house exterior in Houston and Sugar Land is October–November or March–May. Here's how heat, humidity, dew and rain affect the job, and how to paint well in summer.
author: Chris Petkau
content:
Short answer: in Houston, Sugar Land and the rest of Fort Bend County, the best months to paint a house exterior are October through November and March through May. Temperatures sit in the 60s to 80s, humidity is lower than in summer, and there are fewer afternoon storms. You can still get a good result in summer or a mild winter. It just takes more careful scheduling of each day.

What Weather Actually Does to Exterior Paint

Paint doesn't care about the month. It cares about four conditions while it goes on and while it cures over the first day or two:

  • Air and surface temperature. Most standard exterior acrylics need at least 50°F. Many premium lines can be applied down to about 35°F. Always check the product's label. Surface temperature matters as much as air temperature: siding in direct Texas sun can run 30–40°F hotter than the air.

  • Humidity and dew point. High humidity slows drying. If the surface cools to the dew point before the paint sets, moisture condenses on the fresh film. That can leave surfactant streaks (sticky, tan or shiny runs), especially on darker colors.

  • Rain. Most acrylic exterior paints need a few dry hours before rain. The exact window depends on the product and the temperature.

  • Direct sun and wind. Paint applied to a hot, sunny wall skins over too fast. That causes lap marks, poor flow and weaker adhesion.

Houston-Area Exterior Painting, Season by Season

Fall (October–November): the best window

Daytime highs drop into the 70s and 80s, humidity eases, and hurricane season winds down (it officially runs June 1 through November 30). Fall is the most forgiving season for exterior work, which also makes it the busiest. Book early if you want a fall start.

Spring (March–May): a close second

Spring brings similar temperatures, but more rain and pollen. Expect a few weather days built into the schedule. Pollen and dust should be washed off before painting, which is one reason pressure washing is part of every exterior prep.

Summer (June–September): doable with the right schedule

Highs in the 90s, heavy humidity and pop-up afternoon storms make summer the hardest season, not an impossible one. A good crew handles it by:

  • Starting early and following the shade around the house, so no wall is painted while it's sitting in full sun

  • Stopping each day early enough for the film to set before evening dew

  • Watching the radar and holding off when storms are close

  • Choosing products rated for hot, humid conditions

Winter (December–February): often fine on mild days

Many Houston winter days reach the 60s, which is workable. The limits are cold snaps and cold, damp mornings. Short winter days also leave less drying time before dew forms at night.

Timing Matters Less Than Prep

Paint jobs in our area rarely fail because of the month they were done in. They fail because of what happened before the first coat: dirty or chalky siding, failed caulk, bare wood left unprimed, or moisture trapped in stucco. Good weather won't save a poorly prepped surface. Careful prep can make a summer job last as long as a fall one. See how we approach it in our exterior preparation process.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the best month to paint a house exterior in Houston?

October is usually the best single month. Temperatures are moderate, humidity is lower, and storm activity is dropping off. March through May is the next best window.

Can you paint a house exterior in a Houston summer?

Yes. The crew needs to start early, keep paint off walls in full sun, stop before evening dew, and stay ahead of afternoon storms.

How hot is too hot to paint outside?

It depends on the product. Many exterior paints list a maximum surface temperature around 90°F, and a sunny wall can pass that well before the air does. That's why summer work follows the shade.

How long does exterior paint need before it rains?

Most acrylic exterior paints need a few dry hours to become rain-resistant. Cool, humid weather stretches that time. Check the product data sheet for the exact figure.

How far ahead should I book an exterior painter in Sugar Land?

For a fall start, reach out in late summer. Spring and fall are the busiest seasons for exterior work in Fort Bend County.
